verses.text: This is the vision the prophet Habakkuk received.
LORD, how long must I call for help before you listen? I cry out, “Violence!” but you don’t come to rescue.
Why do you make me watch evil and look at trouble? Destruction and violence surround me; arguments break out and conflict keeps rising.
The law has lost its force, and justice never wins. The wicked close in on the righteous, so justice comes out twisted.
“Look among the nations. Watch closely and be amazed, because I am doing something in your own days that you would not believe, even if someone told you.
“I am raising up the Chaldeans, a fierce, restless nation that sweeps across the earth and takes homes that belong to others.
“They inspire fear and terror. They make their own rules and claim their own honor.
“Their horses are faster than leopards and fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their riders charge forward; they come from far away, swooping like an eagle diving for prey.
“They all come intent on violence. Their troops advance in a line, and they collect captives like sand.
“They ridicule kings and laugh at rulers. They mock every fortress, piling up earth against its walls and capturing it.
“Then they sweep past like the wind. They are guilty, because they treat their own strength as a god.”
LORD my God, my Holy One, haven’t you always existed? We will not die. LORD, you appointed them to bring judgment; Rock, you established them to punish.
Your eyes are too pure to look approvingly at evil; you cannot accept wrongdoing. So why do you tolerate traitors? Why stay silent while the wicked swallow up people more righteous than themselves?
Why do you let people become like fish in the sea, like small creatures with no ruler over them?
The enemy hooks them, hauls them in with a net, and gathers them in a dragnet. Then he celebrates and cheers.
That is why he offers sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet: he credits them for his rich life and excellent food.
Will he keep emptying his net and killing nations without mercy?
